transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I keep going back over my work, over and over. Like after a job I’ll check the breakers, the labels, torque marks, photos I took—sometimes I’ll even drive back to the site to look again. A simple install ends up taking way longer than it should, and people are starting to notice.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you try to focus on something else?

Yes. Even after I know I checked a panel or a disconnect, the thought keeps coming back that maybe I missed something—like one loose neutral—or left something that could start a fire. I try to push it out of my head, but it follows me all the way home.
Do you feel like you have to check things in a specific way or a certain number of times to feel okay about them?

Yeah. It’s not always a set number, exactly, but I have to go back through things in a certain way before I can let it go. I’ll recheck the breakers, the labels, the torque marks, then look over the photos I took. Sometimes that still doesn’t feel like enough, and I’ll end up driving back to the site to check in person. It makes jobs take way longer than they should.
Do you feel like your checking is done to prevent something bad from happening?

Yes. That’s the main reason I keep doing it. I’ll think, what if I missed a breaker label, or the torque wasn’t right, or something gets overlooked and causes a problem later. So I go back through the job, check the photos, and sometimes even drive back to the site just to make sure nothing bad happens.
Do you feel like you have to do your checks in a particular order to feel like they're done correctly?

Yeah, pretty much. I feel like I have to go back over the job in the same sort of sequence—breakers, labels, torque marks, then the photos—otherwise it doesn’t feel finished in my head. If I skip around, I start thinking I might’ve missed something, and then I end up checking it all again. Sometimes it gets to the point where a simple install takes way longer than it should, and people are starting to notice.
Do you feel like you have to arrange things in a symmetrical or perfect way, or is it more about making sure everything is correct and not making a mistake?

It’s more about making sure everything is correct and that I didn’t make a mistake. I’m not really trying to make things look symmetrical or perfect. I just keep going back over the job—breakers, labels, torque marks, the photos—because I’m worried I missed something. Sometimes I even drive back to the site, and then a simple install ends up taking way too long. People are starting to notice.
Do you feel anxious or fearful when you think about not checking things as you normally do?

Yes, I do. If I think about not doing the checks the way I usually do, I get really uneasy. It feels like something might slip through, like I missed a breaker or a label or didn’t catch something in the photos. That anxiety is what makes me go back over it again, and sometimes it gets to the point where I’m spending way too long on what should be a simple job.
Do you feel like your checking behaviors are aimed at preventing harm to yourself or others?

Yeah, I think so. It’s not like I’m scared something will happen to me personally, but if I miss something on a job, it could matter. So I keep going back over the breakers, labels, torque marks, the photos... sometimes I even drive back to the site. I know it’s taking way longer than it should, but in the moment it feels like I have to be sure.
Do you feel like your need to check things is interfering with your work or daily activities?

Yes, it is. My schedule is starting to slip because jobs I should be finishing in one visit turn into callbacks or extra checking. It’s costing me time, and I can tell some clients are losing confidence a bit.

It also affects the apprentices, because I’m tied up rechecking instead of spending time with them. And after work, I’ve been skipping things I used to enjoy because I’m still reviewing the job in my head or worrying I might need to go back.
Do you feel distressed or upset when you're unable to perform your checking behaviors?

Yes. If I can’t do the checks, I get really bothered by it. I keep thinking about the breakers, the labels, the torque marks, the photos—like maybe I missed something. Even after I leave a site, it can sit in my head until I go back or check again somehow. It’s frustrating, because I know a simple install shouldn’t take that long, but I feel pretty upset if I’m not able to make sure.
Are you avoiding certain work assignments or social situations because of your need to check things?

Yeah, I’ve been avoiding some things. Work-wise, I’m not exactly turning down every job, but my schedule is slipping because jobs that should be done in one visit turn into extra checks or callbacks. It’s starting to cost me time, and I think some clients notice.

And outside of work, I’ve been skipping things I used to do after hours because I’m still thinking through a job or wondering if I need to go back and check something. It’s been getting in the way more than I’d like.
Is your main concern when checking things that you might have made a mistake, or that something bad could happen as a result of your work?

It’s mostly that something bad could happen because I missed a mistake. Like even after I know I checked a panel or a disconnect, this thought keeps barging in that maybe I missed one loose neutral or left something unsafe.

I try to tell myself I already checked it, but then I start thinking, what if it starts a fire? And that thought can follow me all the way home.
Is your fear of something bad happening related to a specific type of accident or problem, like an electrical fire?

Yes, mainly an electrical fire. I’ll check a panel or a disconnect and know I looked at it, but then this thought comes back that maybe I missed one loose neutral or left something unsafe. I try to push it out of my mind, but it can follow me all the way home.

It’s more about preventing what could happen because of a mistake. I’m not just worried about being wrong on paper or looking bad.

That’s why I keep going back over the same things—breakers, labels, torque marks, photos. Sometimes I’ll even drive back to a site to check again. A simple install ends up taking way longer than it should, and people are starting to notice.

It’s what might happen because of the mistake. Like, even if I know I checked the panel or the disconnect, I get this thought that maybe I missed a loose neutral or left something unsafe. Then my mind goes right to, what if that starts a fire?

I try to shake it off, but it’ll keep coming back, even after I’ve left the job. Sometimes it follows me all the way home.
